rendered: The premise is not what the paper says. It does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]. It reports the lithium leaching as small: the paper states that even Ni-rich NMC 811 shows only minimal[2] leaching (~3 wt%) after one week[3]. Its overall conclusion is the reverse of the premise: Overall, this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is[4] compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[5]. The paper does flag a real concern: Li+/H+ exchange during water exposure raises the pH, which can corrode the aluminum current collector. It treats this as a problem to manage rather than a barrier. It notes that the capacity retention of aqueous-processed cells is slightly lower than that of NMP-processed cells (~70% vs. ~76%)[6], and that this could be improved by changing the formulation and by compensating for the pH rise.
